summary: Off-registry HTTPS tarball dependency smuggles unpinned code into install
details: sc-geeksquad-core@99.9.1 declares its only dependency `ltidisafe` as a direct HTTPS tarball URL (`https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-3.9.7.tgz`) in package.json rather than a registry version range. On `npm install`, npm fetches those bytes from the external bucket with no registry resolution, no version pin, and no integrity hash, and executes any lifecycle scripts contained in that tarball. The shipped index.js is an empty stub, so the manifest line is the entire effective payload of this package. The package name resembles the `sc-geeksquad` namespace and the implausibly high version (99.9.1) is consistent with a dependency-confusion/resolution-winning shape against an internal package of a similar name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
